investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (the resource was at or above its allocatable limit), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~143 s before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a hard contract failure. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all allocatable VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely] Node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a specific node pool or label set that only covers the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes; those nodes are saturated, so the pod cannot fall back to the other 4 nodes.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a higher count to 2, shrinking total VM capacity below the demand level at the time of the eval run.

[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node is configured lower than the actual concurrent demand from simultaneous eval runs (all three sibling checks ran within the same ~7-minute window and each requested a VM slot).

[Less likely] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more than 1 unit) could exhaust a node's quota with a single pod, but the scheduler message says 'Insufficient' rather than 'request exceeds capacity', which is more consistent with aggregate exhaustion.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-26T12:29–12:34Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" as its first step (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), the pod for the remote agent VM was never scheduled, so no agent was created and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the contract validation to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler cannot place the peer-pod VM required to create a remote agent, so every remote-agent eval times out unscheduled (~142–146 s) and returns no evidence. This is an infrastructure capacity or node-selector misconfiguration issue localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet; this is an eval-layer failure that reflects the state of the production Kubernetes cluster at the time of the run.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing peer-pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption is also blocked ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are at capacity. A misconfiguration of node selectors or a node label change could have reduced the eligible node pool.
TERTIARY — Cluster-level resource quota or limit range preventing new kata peer-pod VMs from being admitted even if node capacity were available.

UNLIKELY — Eval runner misconfiguration causing it to submit pods to the wrong namespace or with incorrect resource requests; however, the scheduler message is specific to kata.peerpods.io/vm insufficiency, not a generic admission error.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (the resource was at or above its allocatable limit), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~143 s before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a hard contract failure. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all allocatable VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely] Node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a specific node pool or label set that only covers the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes; those nodes are saturated, so the pod cannot fall back to the other 4 nodes.

[Possible] A recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a higher count to 2, shrinking total VM capacity below the demand level at the time of the eval run.

[Possible] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node is configured lower than the actual concurrent demand from simultaneous eval runs (all three sibling checks ran within the same ~7-minute window and each requested a VM slot).

[Less likely] A misconfiguration in the pod's resource request for kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., requesting more than 1 unit) could exhaust a node's quota with a single pod, but the scheduler message says 'Insufficient' rather than 'request exceeds capacity', which is more consistent with aggregate exhaustion.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-26T12:29–12:34Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" as its first step (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), the pod for the remote agent VM was never scheduled, so no agent was created and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the contract validation to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler cannot place the peer-pod VM required to create a remote agent, so every remote-agent eval times out unscheduled (~142–146 s) and returns no evidence. This is an infrastructure capacity or node-selector misconfiguration issue localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet; this is an eval-layer failure that reflects the state of the production Kubernetes cluster at the time of the run.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are at capacity. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-06-26 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or invoking the runtime, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~142–147 s), preventing agent creation and all downstream eval steps. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval pipeline.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=150553, pod stuck unscheduled for 146s before eval timeout.
sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=150968, pod stuck 143s — failed before remote-agent-runtime run began.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=146061, pod stuck 142s — failed before remote-agent-runtime run began.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent because pod never scheduled and agent was never created.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence was captured at any stage of the probe.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) as the first substantive step; scheduling failure prevents this call from completing.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the 150553ms latency is well within the outage threshold, confirming the failure is scheduling-driven not a timeout misconfiguration.
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes — no capacity available for new remote-agent pods and preemption found no victims to evict.
Secondary: A prior eval run or other workload left orphaned remote-agent pods running on the 2 eligible nodes, consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and blocking new scheduling.

Tertiary: The node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods restricts scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, creating a narrow capacity ceiling that is easily saturated; the remaining 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of available resources.

Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event (node drain, node failure, or autoscaler scale-down) reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent eval probes — no node health signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm or deny this.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same unschedulable pod message if capacity is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three failing remote-agent checks together to confirm shared scheduling bottleneck
reproductionSteps.details: All three checks should reproduce the same kata.peerpods.io/vm Unschedulable message if the root cause is cluster-wide capacity exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current pod scheduling state on the production cluster
reproductionSteps.details: Use cluster tooling (kubectl or equivalent) to list pending remote-agent pods and describe their scheduling events to confirm the Unschedulable reason matches the eval message.

reproductionSteps.label: Check allocatable and used kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Describe each of the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod affinity to see current allocatable vs. requested kata.peerpods.io/vm counts and identify which pods are holding the slots.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agent pod scheduling — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on production Kubernetes cluster
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages explicitly names Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on 2 nodes as the blocking condition.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185) failed with the same scheduling error in the same eval run window, indicating the shared pod scheduling layer is the common failure point.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent remote path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote'; this call cannot complete when the underlying pod cannot be scheduled, leaving all required evidence fields uncollected.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: Contract at lines 266–270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message; all five are missing because the scheduling failure prevents any agent lifecycle step from executing.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-eligible nodes immediately to determine current slot usage and identify which pods are holding capacity.

Check for orphaned or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916); terminate any such pods to free slots.

Assess whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit on the 2 eligible nodes can be increased, or whether additional nodes with the required affinity labels can be added to the cluster to expand capacity.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods to determine whether the 4 currently ineligible nodes could be made eligible, which would increase the scheduling surface from 2 to up to 6 nodes.

After restoring capacity, re-run all three remote-agent eval checks to confirm they pass and produce the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) with the message assertion 'hello from aura' satisfied.

Consider adding a pre-flight cluster capacity check to the eval runner that reports available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before attempting agent creation, to surface exhaustion earlier with a clearer diagnostic message.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe to check if scheduling failure persists
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is ongoing or was transient at the time of the original run.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Describe the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-eligible nodes to inspect current resource allocation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether slots are still exhausted and which pods are holding them.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl describe node on each of the 2 nodes matching the remote-agent pod affinity and check the Allocatable and Requests fields for kata.peerpods.io/vm.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List all pending and running remote-agent pods on the production cluster
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether a prior eval run or other workload left pods that are blocking new scheduling.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run kubectl get pods with a label selector for remote-agent workloads across all namespaces to identify any orphaned or stuck pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check node affinity/selector rules for remote-agent pods against all 6 cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the 4-node exclusion is intentional or a misconfiguration that is artificially constraining capacity.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Retrieve the pod spec for a failing remote-agent pod and compare its nodeAffinity/nodeSelector against the labels on all 6 nodes to confirm only 2 are eligible.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agent sibling checks together after any remediation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Validates that all three checks pass end-to-end once scheduling capacity is restored, confirming the shared dependency was the sole failure point.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes scheduler events for the failing pods showed a reason other than Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., image pull failure, OOMKilled, API auth error), the capacity-exhaustion diagnosis would not hold.

If kubectl describe on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run, the root cause would shift to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration or a scheduler bug rather than capacity exhaustion.
If a concurrent re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and produced all 5 required evidence fields, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' were shown to actually have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the affinity rules were recently changed to exclude them, the root cause would be a node affinity misconfiguration rather than raw capacity exhaustion.

If no remote-agent pods were found running or pending on the cluster at the time of failure, it would suggest the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit is set too low in the node configuration rather than being consumed by live workloads.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, failing fast with a capacity-specific message rather than waiting for the pod scheduling timeout.
Add a stale-pod cleanup eval that detects and reports remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold that may be orphaned and consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod affinity/selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3 eligible nodes), alerting before capacity is fully exhausted.
Consider a regression eval that tracks kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization over time to detect trending exhaustion before it causes scheduling failures.

evidenceDigest.message: pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.
